Rashi on Shabbat 124a:10:1.hebrew: לרבה אליבא דרבי נחמיה - דאמר דבר שמלאכתו להיתר, לצורך מקומו לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:10:1.english: According to Rabba in accordance with Rabbi Neḥemya - Who said [that] an object whose [primary] function is for a permitted [use] [may] not [be moved] for the need of its place.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:10:2.hebrew: הני קערות - לאחר אכילה, היכי מטלטל להו לסלקן מלפנינו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:10:2.english: These bowls - After eating, how does one carry them to remove them from before us?

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:12:1.hebrew: ואם לאו אין מטלטלין אותה - בשלמא לרבה, כגון דאין צריך לגופה [אלא למקומה], אלא לדידך אמאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:12:1.english: And if not, one may not move it - It is well according to Rabbah, [as it refers to] a case where one does not need [the utensil] itself, [but rather its place]; however, according to you, why [is it prohibited]?

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:13:1.hebrew: וכן בדלת - אוקימנא במסכת ביצה, וכן הדלת אין סומכין בבקעת, וביו"ט קיימי:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:13:1.english: And so too, a door - We established in Tractate Beitzah [that this means]: "and so too, one may not prop the door with a piece of wood," and they [these laws] are dealing with a Festival.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:13:2.hebrew: והא בקעת ביו"ט מלאכתה להיתר היא - דלהסקה חזי וקיימא, וקאסר לטלטלה לצורך גופו למלאכה אחרת, וכל שכן לצורך מקומה. ומשני: התם טעמא, כיון דבשבת אסור — דהא בקעת בשבת מלאכתה לאיסור היא — ביום טוב נמי אסור, גזירה יו"ט אטו שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:13:2.english: And isn't a piece of wood on a Festival [an object whose] function is for a permitted [use] - For it is fit and designated for kindling, and [the Mishnah] prohibits moving it for the need of [the object] itself for another task, and all the more so for the need of its place. And [the Gemara] answers: There, the reason [is that] since on Shabbat it is prohibited — for on Shabbat a piece of wood's function is for a prohibited [use] — on a Festival it is also prohibited, [as] a decree [concerning] a Festival on account of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:15:1.hebrew: משילין פירות דרך ארובה ביום טוב - בהדיא תנן: אבל לא בשבת. פירות השטוחים על הגג לייבשן, וראה גשמים ממשמשים ובאין, משילן לארץ דרך ארובת הגג, דלא טריחא מילתא, דנופלין מאליהן; אלמא דלא גזרינן. ופרכינן: ומי לא גזרינן? והתנן: אין בין כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:15:1.english: One may drop fruits through a skylight on a Festival - We explicitly learned [in the Mishnah]: "but not on Shabbat." [The case is] fruits that are spread out on the roof to dry, and one saw rain approaching: one drops them to the ground through the skylight of the roof, because it is not a laborious matter, as they fall on their own; apparently, we do not issue a decree [prohibiting an act on a Festival due to Shabbat]. And we ask: Do we not issue a decree? Didn't we learn: "There is no [difference] between [a Festival and Shabbat]," etc.?

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:17:1.hebrew: לא קשיא הא - דתנן משילין, דשרי טירחא ביו"ט משום איבוד ממון, רבי יהושע היא, שהתיר להעלות בהמה בהערמה מן הבור:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:17:1.english: [This is] not difficult; this - [the Mishnah] that we learned, "One may lower [produce]," which permits exertion on a Festival due to financial loss, is [the opinion of] Rabbi Yehoshua, who permitted raising an animal from a pit through artifice.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:17:2.hebrew: והא - דתנן אין בין כו', ר"א היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:17:2.english: And this - [i.e.,] what we learned [in the Mishnah]: "There is no [difference] between [a Festival and Shabbat]..." etc. — is [the opinion of] Rabbi Eliezer.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:19:1.hebrew: דאפשר בהערמה - דמיחזי כמאן דעביד לצורך יו"ט, אבל גבי משילין, דליכא הערמה לדמויי להתירא — לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:19:1.english: Where it is possible [to employ] artifice - For it appears like one who is acting for the need of the festival; but regarding lowering [produce], where there is no artifice to make it resemble a permitted [act], no.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:1:1.english: His hand on his fellow’s shoulder - Because they do not move sticks [on Shabbat].

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:2:1.hebrew: גלוסטרא - דתנן רבי יהושע אמר, נגר שיש בראשו גלוסטרא — שראשה עב, וראוי לדוך בו שום, ונועלין בו דלת:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:2:1.english: Gelostra - As we learned [in the Mishnah], Rabbi Yehoshua said, "A bolt that has a gelostra at its head" — [meaning] its head is thick, and it is fit for crushing garlic with it, and one locks a door with it.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:2:2.hebrew: שומטה מפתח זה ותולה בחברו - ואע"ג דצריך לגופו לתלותו בחברו ולנועלה בו, שומטו ע"י גרירה, אבל טלטול גמור לא. ואע"פ שמלאכתו להיתר, לא שרי ליה לצורך גופו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:2:2.english: One removes it from this doorway and hangs it in another - Even though he needs it for its own use, to hang it in another [doorway] and lock [the door] with it, he removes it by dragging, but complete carrying [is] not [permitted]. And even though its [primary] function is for a permitted [purpose], [Rabbi Yehoshua] does not permit it [to be carried] for its own use.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:3:1.hebrew: מדוכה הא דאמרן - לעיל. אע"ג דשנייה רבא לעיל מחמה לצל, ואביי שנייה לצורך מקומו, שינויי דחיקי נינהו; אלא קודם התרת כלים נשנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:3:1.english: A mortar, that which we said - Above. Even though Rava answered it above [as referring to moving it] from the sun to the shade, and Abaye answered it [as referring to] needing its place, they are forced answers; rather, they were taught prior to the permitting of utensils.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:3:2.english: Rods, what is the reason - [that] they arrange them in the stack [of showbread]?

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:3:3.hebrew: משום איעפושי - דלא סמכינן אניסא, ומשום ההוא פורתא — שהישנה מתעכבת בלא קנים מלילי שבת לשבת, והחדשה משבת למוצ"ש — לא מיעפשי:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:3:3.english: Due to [concern of] decay - For we do not rely on a miracle, and because of that brief [interval] — when the old [showbread] remains without rods from Shabbat eve until Shabbat [day], and the new [showbread] from Shabbat [day] until the conclusion of Shabbat — they do not decay.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:3:4.hebrew: כדר"א - מניח ידו על כתף חבירו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:3:4.english: Like [that of] Rabbi Elazar - [One] places his hand on his fellow's shoulder.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:4:1.hebrew: שאינה מעורבת - שהרבה בתים פתוחים לה ולא עירבו. דכלים ששבתו בבתים אסור להוציאן לחצר, וששבתו בחצר מותר לטלטלן בחצר, שהחצר כולו רשות לעצמו הוא, והבתים מיוחדים לכל איש ביתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:4:1.english: That is not joined [by an eiruv] - For many houses open into it and they did not make an eiruv. For utensils that rested [at the onset of Shabbat] in the houses are forbidden to be taken out into the courtyard, whereas [those] that rested in the courtyard are permitted to be carried in the courtyard, because the entire courtyard is a domain unto itself, and the houses are designated [separately], each person [to] his own house.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:4:2.english: Inside the doorway - from where he took the bolt.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:4:3.hebrew: וקא מטלטל מנא דבית בחצר - הלכך, שומטה אין, דטלטול מן הצד היא, אבל טלטול גמור לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:4:3.english: And he is moving a utensil of the house in the courtyard - Therefore, pulling it out — yes, [it is permitted,] because it is indirect moving; however, complete moving — no, [it is prohibited].

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:5:1.hebrew: מדוכה רבי נחמיה היא - דאמר, ובעירובין (דף לה.), אפילו טלית ואפי' תרווד אין ניטלין אלא לצורך תשמיש המיוחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:5:1.english: [With regard to] a mortar, [it] is Rabbi Neḥemya - who says [so], and in Eruvin (35a) [he states that] even a cloak and even a ladle may not be moved except for the purpose of [their] designated use.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:6:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> במתניתין, כל הכלים ניטלין לצורך כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:6:1.english: This is how we read in the Mishnah: "All vessels may be moved for a [specific] purpose," etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:7:1.hebrew: מאי לצורך ומאי שלא לצורך אמר רבה כו' - לצורך דשרי תנא קמא, היינו דבר שמלאכתו להיתר ומטלטלו לצורך גופו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:7:1.english: What [is] "for a purpose" and what [is] "not for a purpose"? Rabbah said, etc. - "For a purpose" that the first Tanna permits is an item whose [designated] use is for a permitted [activity], and one moves it for the need of [using the item] itself.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:8:1.hebrew: שלא לצורך דבר שמלאכתו להיתר - ומטלטלו שלא לצורך גופו, אבל צריך למקומו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:8:1.english: Not for a purpose — an object whose function is for a permitted [use] - And he moves it not for the purpose of [using the object] itself, but [because] he needs its place.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:8:2.hebrew: ודבר שמלאכתו לאיסור לצורך גופו - הוא דאישתראי, אם צריך לו למלאכת היתר; אבל שלא לצורך גופו, ואע"ג דצריך למקומו, לא. ורבה לטעמיה, דאמר לעיל (שבת דף קכב:) גבי קורנס של נפחים נמי מותר לצורך גופו:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:8:2.english: And [an object] whose function is for a prohibited [use], for the purpose of [utilizing] itself - That is what is permitted, if one needs it for a permitted task; but not for the purpose of [utilizing] itself — even though one needs its place — no [it is not permitted]. And Rabbah follows his own reasoning, as he said above (Shabbat 122b) regarding a blacksmith's hammer as well, [that] it is permitted for the purpose of [utilizing] itself.

Rashi on Shabbat 124a:9:1.hebrew: א"ל רבא כו' אלא אמר כו' - ולרבא דמוקי אליבא דרבי נחמיה דלצורך גופו ולצורך מקומו מותר, ע"כ האי לצורך גופו כגון שזה התשמיש מיוחד לו — דתניא לקמן בפרק חבית (שבת שבת דף קמו.): רבי נחמיה אומר, אפילו תרווד ואפילו טלית אין ניטלין אלא לצורך תשמישן — וצורך מקומו נמי לרבא כצורך גופו ותשמישו דמי. ולרבה, צורך גופו הוא דשרי רבי נחמיה, ודוקא לתשמיש המיוחד לו. ובין לרבה ובין לרבא, דוקא דבר שמלאכתו להיתר; אבל דבר שמלאכתו לאיסור, אפילו לצורך גופו לא שרי רבי נחמיה, דהאי צורך גופו לאו תשמיש המיוחד לו הוא, דהא מיוחד למלאכת איסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 124a:9:1.english: Rava said to him, etc. Rather, [Rava] said, etc. - According to Rava, who interprets [the baraita] in accordance with Rabbi Neḥemya that [moving an object] for the purpose of [utilizing] itself and for the purpose of [utilizing] its place is permitted, perforce this "[for the purpose of utilizing] itself" [means] such that this use is specific to it — as it is taught in a baraita below in the chapter [entitled] Chavit (Shabbat 146a): "Rabbi Neḥemya says: Even a ladle and even a cloak may not be moved except for the purpose of their [designated] use" — and [moving an object for] the purpose of its place, too, according to Rava, is like [moving it for] the purpose of itself and its [designated] use. And according to Rabbah, it is [only] for the purpose of itself that Rabbi Neḥemya permits [moving it], and specifically for a use that is specific to it. And both according to Rabbah and according to Rava, [this applies] specifically to an object whose primary function is for a permitted use; however, [regarding] an object whose primary function is for a prohibited use, even for the purpose of itself Rabbi Neḥemya does not permit [moving it], because this "purpose of itself" is not a use that is specific to it, since it is designated for a prohibited function.

Tosafot on Shabbat 124a:17:1.hebrew: הא ר"א - ההיא ד"אין בין", אע"ג דבפ"ק דמגילה (דף ז:) דייקינן עלה: "הא לענין מכשירי אוכל נפש — זה וזה שוין", וקאמר מתני' דלא כרבי יהודה, ור"א סבירא ליה כר"י ועדיפא מדרבי יהודה כדאמר בריש תולין (לקמן שבת דף קלז:) — איכא למימר דההוא תנא סבר לה כוותיה בחדא, דגזרינן י"ט אטו שבת, ופליג עליה במכשירין. ועוד יש לומר, ד"אין בין" דפ"ק דמגילה מיירי במילי דאורייתא, ו"אין בין" דהכא היינו דתנן במשילין (ביצה ד' לז:) דמיירי במילי דשבות, ואינו מענין אחד. תדע, דהכי פריך עלה בפ' משילין כדפריך הכא בשמעתא, ולא פריך בפ"ק דמגילה; והא דדייק התם: "הא לענין מכשירין — זה וזה שוין", לא דייק בפרק משילין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 124a:17:1.english: This [is] Rabbi Eliezer - [With regard to] that [mishna] of "There is no [difference] between [a Festival and Shabbat]": even though in the first chapter of Megillah (7b) we infer from it, "Thus, with respect to preliminaries for food preparation, this and that [i.e., a Festival and Shabbat] are equal," and [the Gemara] states that the Mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda — whereas Rabbi Eliezer holds like Rabbi Yehuda, and even goes further than Rabbi Yehuda, as stated at the beginning of [chapter] Tolin (below, Shabbat 137b) — one can say that that Tanna agrees with him in one [matter], namely that we issue a decree on a Festival on account of Shabbat, and disagrees with him regarding preliminaries [for food preparation]. Furthermore, one can say that "There is no [difference] between" of the first chapter of Megillah deals with biblical matters, whereas "There is no [difference] between" here is that which we learned in [the chapter] Mashilin (Beitzah 37b), which deals with rabbinic prohibitions [shevut], and it is not the same subject. Know [that this is so], for it raises the same difficulty against it in the chapter Mashilin as it raises here in [our] sugya, and it does not raise [that difficulty] in the first chapter of Megillah; and that which it infers there, "Thus, with respect to preliminaries, this and that are equal," it does not infer in the chapter Mashilin.

Tosafot on Shabbat 124a:2:1.hebrew: הרי היא ככל הכלים - אע"ג דקודם התרת כלים נשנית, איכא למימ': "ככל הכלים" — כעין כוסות וקערות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 124a:2:1.english: It is like all the utensils - Even though [this Mishnah] was taught before the permitting of utensils, one can say [that] "like all the utensils" [means] like cups and bowls.
